definitions.explanation: The action of two or more things happening in turn, one after another in a repeating pattern. Most commonly used adverbially with に as {交互|こうご}に.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}と{白|しろ}を{交互|こうご}に{並|なら}べた。
examples.english: I arranged the red and white ones alternately.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}は{交互|こうご}に{質問|しつもん}に{答|こた}えながら、インタビューを{進|すす}めた。
examples.english: The two of them advanced the interview, taking turns answering questions.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used with に as {交互|こうご}に (alternately, in turn). Can modify verbs to describe any action done in alternation between two or more parties or elements.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {交互|こうご}に{見|み}る (to look back and forth)
- {交互|こうご}に{繰|く}り{返|かえ}す (to alternate repeatedly)
- {左右|さゆう}{交互|こうご}に (alternating left and right)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {交代|こうたい}: taking turns — focuses on replacing one person/thing with another
- {順番|じゅんばん}に: in order, in sequence — more general sequential ordering
